solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Paper needs right editor — most important position

parts.note: the top is the most important position in any ranking

explanation.surface: A newspaper needs a sharp editor in charge to stay at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: A RED-TOP is a British tabloid newspaper, named for its red masthead.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is a British tabloid, so it is a kind of newspaper.

clue.text: Army set up in new regime? Leave the country

indicators.note: in places the turned-up army inside the shuffled regime letters
new signals that the letters of regime are made into something fresh
set up in a down clue means the piece is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Soldiers stage a coup under a new regime, and citizens decide to flee abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the regime letters to EMIGRE and 'set up' turns the army abbreviation upwards; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to depart one's homeland to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: … so leave some presumably to participate

definitions.meaning: a playful reading: if you only grab a portion, you presumably leave the rest behind

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue. Read literally, the phrase means grabbing only a portion, which leaves some behind; as an idiom it means joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part in something is the everyday idiom for participating.

clue.text: Establish command briefly, interrupting foolish talk

indicators.note: interrupting means the shortened command breaks into the middle of the foolish talk

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length

indicators.note: briefly means the command word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: an edict is an official command

explanation.surface: A firm order, quickly given, cuts across idle chatter to settle a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts EDICT to EDIC, which goes 'interrupting' PRATE: PR-EDIC-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to base or found it, which is to establish it on certain grounds.

clue.text: Yellow sea bird half destroyed is beginning to move — it's alive

parts.note: OR is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: half destroyed means only the front half of the bird's name survives

parts.note: a gannet is a large sea bird

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A yellow seabird, half wrecked, starts to stir: it is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half destroyed' keeps GAN of GANNET; 'beginning to' gives M from move. OR is heraldic yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism is any living thing, so it is something that is alive.

clue.text: People in a similar position to be revealed by noon!

definitions.text: People in a similar position to be revealed by noon!

parts.words: People in a similar position to be revealed by noon!
parts.note: counterparts in another organisation; the wordplay hint is that on a clock face at noon the hands point at the top, while the figures facing each other across the dial are the theme

explanation.walkthrough: Counterparts in another body are their opposite numbers; the clock dial at noon suggests figures facing each other across the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's counterpart holding the equivalent post in another organisation is their opposite number.

clue.text: Ferocious females endlessly astonish troubled son

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for astonish loses its last letter

parts.note: to amaze is to astonish

indicators.note: troubled signals the letters of son are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Fierce women endlessly amaze a mother whose son is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims AMAZE to AMAZ; 'troubled' turns SON into ONS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazons of Greek myth were a race of fierce warrior women.

clue.text: Old emperor over several years keeping maiden privately

indicators.note: keeping means the two pieces together hold the maiden between them
over in a down clue places the emperor above the years

parts.note: the Inca was the ruler of the old Peruvian empire
an era is a span of several years
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler spent many years shutting a young woman away in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works because this is a down clue; 'keeping' holds the maiden inside. Maiden as M comes from cricket scoring, an over with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal Latin phrase for proceedings held in private, away from the public.

clue.text: Moon being out illuminated hard stone pillar

indicators.note: being out suggests the letters of moon are out of place and rearranged

parts.note: lit means illuminated
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: With the moon gone, a lit-up hard stone column stands out in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being out' turns MOON into MONO.
explanation.definitionFit: A monolith is a single great block of stone set up as a pillar or monument.

clue.text: I'm at the pharmacy — I'd like a lift!

definitions.meaning: a tonic or restorative drink that one might buy from a chemist
a plea to be collected, read literally as a request to be fetched

explanation.surface: A customer at the chemist's phones home asking to be collected.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick-me-up is a tonic that revives, and literally a request to be collected.

clue.text: Bird to study after autumn abandoning one of the lakes

indicators.note: after places the study piece behind the shortened season
abandoning means the word for autumn drops one of its letters

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
L is the abbreviation for lake, and fall has two of them
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher studies birds after autumn, once the lakes have been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops just one of the two Ls, leaving FAL; 'after' sets the study word behind it. Fall is the American autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Hasten in game after setback to gain cups and medals?

indicators.note: in places the hastening word inside the turned-around game
after setback means the game word is read backwards

parts.note: sport is a game
to hie is an old word for hasten

explanation.surface: Teams must hurry back after a setback in a match to win silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after setback' reverses the game to TROPS, and 'in' puts the archaic word for hurry inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups and medals are examples of trophies, prizes won in competition; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Evening dress beneficial to little Malcolm

parts.note: for means in favour of, beneficial to
Mal is a short form of the name Malcolm

explanation.surface: An evening outfit would do young Malcolm good.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal is an evening gown or dress worn to a formal occasion.

clue.text: Clergy keeping active — sources of power!

indicators.note: keeping means the clergy word holds the active letter inside it

parts.note: rectors are members of the clergy

explanation.surface: Priests who stay busy prove to be real powerhouses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear reactors generate energy, so they are sources of power.

clue.text: Cleric and a ruler in disharmony

indicators.note: in disharmony means the letters are out of tune with their order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A churchman and a monarch are at odds with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disharmony' rearranges AND A RULER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is a Church of England clergyman supervising a group of parishes.

clue.text: The fellow with rubbish picks up a dermatological disorder

indicators.note: picks up means the two pieces gather the letter A between them

parts.note: he refers to a man, the fellow
trash means rubbish

explanation.surface: A man with a pile of rubbish catches a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picks up' has the man and the rubbish gather the A between them, rather than either word swallowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat rash, also called prickly heat, is a skin complaint caused by sweating.

clue.text: Servant not emerging from a factory, might one say?

indicators.note: might one say signals the word is matched by how it is spoken

parts.note: something not factory-produced is made by hand

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what you call goods that never came off a production line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might one say' matches HANDMADE, not mass-produced, with a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a female servant or attendant.

clue.text: Would it be ruined by a pip and peel?

definitions.text: Would it be ruined by a pip and peel?

indicators.note: ruined signals the letters are spoiled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether stray pips and peel would spoil a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges A PIP and PEEL; the whole clue also describes a fruit pie spoilt by bits of fruit left in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie filled with apples might well be spoilt by stray pips and bits of skin.

clue.text: See 15
Refuse to reveal approximately how long one has been around

parts.note: rough means approximate

parts.words: how long one has been around
parts.note: age is how long someone has lived

explanation.surface: Someone declines to reveal roughly how old they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun: roughage is indigestible plant matter in food.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, indigestible matter that passes through as waste, hence refuse.

clue.text: Prosperous region as horrible place for one stranded by the coast?

parts.note: SE is the south-east of England, its wealthiest region
hell is any horrible place

explanation.surface: A wealthy region becomes a hellish place for anyone left stranded at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is south-east England, the most prosperous part of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A seashell is something left stranded on the shore by the tide.

clue.text: No ordeal can upset this genius

indicators.note: can upset says the letters are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: No trial, however hard, can unsettle this brilliant mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can upset' rearranges NO ORDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci is the archetypal Renaissance genius.

clue.text: In Californian city there's a new brown plant

indicators.note: In means the following pieces sit inside the city

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Los Angeles has a fresh brown shrub growing.
explanation.walkthrough: A, N and TAN go 'In' LA: L-ANTAN-A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lantana is a flowering shrub of the verbena family.

clue.text: Dealing out fish at party

parts.note: a do is a party
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone is handing out fish at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Doling is handing out portions, so it means dealing out.

clue.text: Month in which prisoner acquires a second language

indicators.note: in which places the prisoner and his gains inside the month

parts.note: May is a month
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: During one month an inmate picks up a second tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG with A and S goes 'in which' MAY: MA-LAGAS-Y. LAG is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Malagasy is the language of Madagascar.

clue.text: A soft fruit to come on to the market

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A soft fruit goes on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to become available, as a product or book coming out for sale.

clue.text: Very happy about First in English and very slightly drunk?

indicators.note: about means the happy word surrounds the other two pieces

parts.note: elated means very happy

indicators.note: First in means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone on top of the world after coming first in English is also a bit tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: E (from 'First in English') and V go 'about'-ed by ELATED: EL-EV-ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated is a humorous word for slightly drunk, being high in spirits.

clue.text: Athenian inventor's gone back with a great desire unfulfilled

indicators.note: back means the word for gone is read in reverse

parts.note: dead means gone

indicators.note: unfulfilled means the desire is left incomplete, losing its last letter

parts.note: lust is a great desire

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek inventor has retreated with his great ambition unsatisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEAD into DAED; 'unfulfilled' trims LUST to LUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Daedalus was the mythical Athenian craftsman who built the Labyrinth and wings.

clue.text: Bug? One may have a single eye

definitions.meaning: to bug is to annoy or provoke someone

definitions.text: One may have a single eye
definitions.meaning: a sewing implement with one hole for the thread

explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to annoy, and a sewing needle has a single eye.
